item.title: Python Kriging in 2026: GSTools vs PyKrige vs SciKit-GStat Compared
item.description: You have 380 soil-moisture readings scattered across a 40-hectare field, and your boss wants a continuous surface, not dots. Inverse-distance weighting is the obvious first try — and it will quietly invent gradients that do not exist, because it has no concept of spatial correlation. Kriging does: it derives the weights from the data’s own variogram, returns a variance estimate alongside every prediction, and is the only interpolator in this class that is a best linear unbiased predictor.
